statement_short: Hard to describe myself beyond roles or achievements
statement: When someone asks me to describe who I am, I find it difficult to know what to say beyond my roles, responsibilities, or achievements.

statement_short: Unsure what would remain if I lost an important role
statement: When I imagine losing an important role, such as my job, relationship, or position in the family, I am unsure what would remain of my identity.

statement_short: Self-understanding changes with what others say
statement: My understanding of who I am changes considerably depending on what other people say or think about me.

statement_short: Wonder if I truly wanted a decision or followed expectations
statement: After making an important decision, I sometimes wonder, “Did I genuinely want this, or was I influenced by what others expected?”

statement_short: Recognise what makes me different without ranking myself
statement: I can recognise the qualities that make me different from people around me without needing to see myself as better or worse than them.

statement_short: Present very different versions of myself across groups
statement: I notice that I present very different versions of myself depending on whether I am with family, friends, colleagues, or other groups.

statement_short: Copy others to feel accepted
statement: I sometimes copy how other people speak, dress, behave, or express opinions because I want to feel accepted.

statement_short: What I say I want changes with who I talk to
statement: What I say I want can change depending on who I am talking to at the time.

statement_short: Made important choices to avoid disappointing someone
statement: I have made important choices in relationships, work, or life mainly because I did not want to disappoint someone.

statement_short: Know which beliefs are my own even when unpopular
statement: Even when my opinion is unpopular, I can recognise which thoughts and beliefs are genuinely my own.

statement_short: Identify my strengths and limitations without help
statement: I can identify my strengths and limitations without needing someone else to point them out first.

statement_short: First reaction to criticism is to defend myself
statement: When someone criticises me, my first reaction is usually to defend myself rather than consider whether the criticism may be useful.

statement_short: Try to appear strong even when struggling
statement: I try to appear strong and in control, even when I am struggling, uncertain, or in need of help.

statement_short: Pause and examine an unfamiliar description of me
statement: When someone describes me in a way I do not recognise, I can pause and examine their perspective before accepting or rejecting it.

statement_short: Admit I was wrong without being defined by it
statement: I can admit that I was wrong without feeling that the mistake defines who I am.

statement_short: Can name and explain my guiding values
statement: I can name the personal values that guide my decisions and explain why those values matter to me.

statement_short: Recent actions reflect my stated values
statement: Looking back at my recent choices, my actions generally reflect the values I say are important to me.

statement_short: Recognise when behaviour goes against my values
statement: When my behaviour goes against my values, I can recognise the inconsistency instead of immediately justifying it.

statement_short: Identify what triggered a strong emotion
statement: I can usually identify what triggered a strong emotion, such as anger, frustration, fear, jealousy, excitement, or happiness.

statement_short: Make time to examine choices and patterns
statement: I intentionally make time to examine my choices, emotions, and recurring patterns, even when no one else will know that I have done so.

statement_short: Know if an argument protects values or pride
statement: When I am in an argument, I can easily know if it is to protect my values or to protect my pride.
